extracted.intended_audience: students of law, legal educators, and practitioners seeking foundational principles of law and legal education
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of the nature and classifications of law (natural, revealed, law of nations, municipal) together with rules governing a university legal benefaction (eligibility, residence, forfeiture, elections) and recommended method for teaching law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellow election and eligibility (Mr Viner's foundation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every fellow be elected by convocation, and at the time of election be unmarried, and at least a master of arts or bachelor of civil law, and a member of some college or hall in the university of Oxford; the scholars of this foundation or such as have been scholars (if qualified and approved of by convocation) to have the preference: that, if not a barrister when chosen, he be called to the bar within one year after his election; but do reside in the university two months in every year, or in case of non-residence do forfeit the stipend of that year to Mr Viner's general fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies eligibility, preference, qualification (degree), professional progress (call to the bar within 1 year if not already), and an annual residence requirement (two months) with financial forfeiture as sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholar election and progression requirements (Mr Viner's scholarships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every scholar be elected by convocation, and at the time of election be unmarried, and a member of some college or hall in the university of Oxford, who shall have been matriculated twenty four calendar months at the least: that he do take the degree of bachelor of civil law with all convenient speed; and previous to his taking the same, between the second and eighth year from his matriculation, be bound to attend two courses of the professor's lectures, to be certified under the professor's hand; and within one year after taking the same be called to the bar: that he do annually reside six months till he is of four years standing, and four months from that time till he is master of arts or bachelor of civil law; after which he be bound to reside two months in every year; or, in case of non-residence, do forfeit the stipend of that year to Mr Viner's general fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets minimum matriculation time, degree-taking timeline, mandatory attendance on professor's lectures (with certification), deadline to be called to the bar, graduated residence obligations tied to standing, and forfeiture sanction for non-residence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes and procedures for voiding fellowships and scholarships
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarships become void in case of non-attendance on the professor, or not taking the degree of bachelor of civil law, being duly admonished so to do by the vice-chancellor and proctors: and both fellowships and scholarships do expire at the end of ten years after each respective election; and become void in case of gross misbehaviour, non-residence for two years together, marriage, not being called to the bar within the time before limited, (being duly admonished so to be by the vice-chancellor and proctors) or deserting the profession of the law by following any other profession: and that in any of these cases the vice-chancellor, with consent of convocation, do declare the place actually void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific grounds (non-attendance, failure to take degree after admonition, gross misconduct, prolonged non-residence, marriage, failure to be called to bar after admonition, deserting profession) and prescribes administrative declaration by vice-chancellor with convocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vacancy handling and notice for elections
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of any vacancy of the professorship, fellowships, or scholarships, the profits of the current year be ratably divided between the predecessor or his representatives, and the successor; and that a new election be had within one month afterwards, unless by that means the time of election shall fall within any vacation, in which case it be deferred to the first week in the next full term. And that before any convocation shall be held for such election, or for any other matter relating to Mr Viner's benefaction, ten days public notice be given to each college and hall of the convocation, and the cause of convoking it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes interim profit-sharing, prompt timing for new elections (with vacation exception), and a minimum ten-day public notice to colleges and halls specifying cause before convocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universities as prerequisite foundation for legal training
rubrics_metrics.description: The leisure and abilities of the learned in these retirements might ... improve its method ... If ever this study should arrive to any tolerable perfection either here or at Cambridge, the nobility and gentry of this kingdom would not shorten their residence upon this account ... the student in our laws hath formed both his sentiments and style, by perusal and imitation of the purest classical writers ... a student thus qualified may enter upon the study of the law with incredible advantage and reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative argument that academical education should precede professional legal training; emphasizes benefits to method, reputation, and the quality of the profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exclusive practical/apprenticeship-only education
rubrics_metrics.description: The custom ... to drop all liberal education, as of no use to lawyers; and to place them ... at the desk of some skilful attorney ... If practice be the whole he is taught, practice must also be the whole he will ever know: if he be uninstructed in the elements and first principles upon which the rule of practice is founded, the least variation from established precedents will totally distract and bewilder him ... he must never aspire to form, and seldom expect to comprehend, any arguments drawn a priori, from the spirit of the laws and the natural foundations of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques education that focuses solely on mechanical practice; prescribes grounding in elements and first principles to enable reasoning beyond precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired intellectual curriculum for law students
rubrics_metrics.description: The student ... if he can reason with precision, and separate argument from fallacy, by the clear simple rules of pure unsophisticated logic; if he can fix his attention, and steadily pursue truth ... by the use of mathematical demonstrations; if he has enlarged his conceptions of nature and art, by a view of the several branches of genuine, experimental, philosophy; if he has impressed on his mind the sound maxims of the law of nature ... if, lastly, he has contemplated those maxims reduced to a practical system in the laws of imperial Rome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends a broad liberal curriculum (classical literature, logic, mathematics, natural philosophy, natural law, Roman law) as preparation for legal study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired moral and civic qualities in a lawyer
rubrics_metrics.description: Affectionate loyalty to the king, a zeal for liberty and the constitution, a sense of real honour, and well grounded principles of religion; as necessary to form a truly valuable English lawyer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States character virtues (loyalty, zeal for liberty/constitution, honour, religion) as essential complements to intellectual training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended method of instruction (the expositor's role)
rubrics_metrics.description: He should consider his course as a general map of the law, marking out the shape of the country, its connexions and boundaries, its greater divisions and principal cities: it is not his business to describe minutely the subordinate limits ... His attention should be engaged ... in tracing out the originals and as it were the elements of the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers should provide high-level structure (map), trace legal origins to fountains (customs, Roman codes, feudal law), explain by reasons, illustrate with examples, cite authorities, deduce history and changes, and show connections with other systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary pedagogy for beginners (avoid overloading)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the tender understanding of the student be loaded at the first with a multitude and variety of matter, it will either occasion him to desert his studies, or will carry him heavily through them ... teach in a light and simple way at first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates starting from simple, essential elements and avoiding overwhelming beginners with excessive detail; adapt attention required to branches of law according to student aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of law (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Law ... signifies a rule of action; and is applied indiscriminately to all kinds of action ... It is that rule of action, which is prescribed by some superior, and which the inferior is bound to obey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames law broadly (physical, moral, civil) but emphasizes prescription by a superior and obligation of inferior as central features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of nature (content and authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: This will of his maker is called the law of nature ... he laid down only such laws as were founded in those relations of justice ... the eternal, immutable laws of good and evil ... Such among others are these principles: that we should live honestly, should hurt nobody, and should render to every one his due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presents law of nature as divine, eternal, discoverable by reason to an extent, superior to human laws, and foundational for other legal systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revealed (divine) law and relation to natural law
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctrines thus delivered we call the revealed or divine law, and they are to be found only in the holy scriptures. These precepts, when revealed, are found upon comparison to be really a part of the original law of nature ... the revealed law is (humanly speaking) of infinitely more authority than what we generally call the natural law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes revealed law (scriptural) as authoritative and often clarifying truths not attainable by corrupted human reason alone; still aligned with natural law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of nations (basis and construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: A third kind of law to regulate this mutual intercourse, called 'the law of nations;' which ... depends entirely upon the rules of natural law, or upon mutual compacts, treaties, leagues, and agreements between these several communities: in the construction also of which compacts we have no other rule to resort to, but the law of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains international law as grounded in natural law or consensual compacts between states; uses natural law as interpretive rule for treaties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of municipal (civil) law and its essential properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Municipal law ... is properly defined to be 'a rule of civil conduct prescribed by the supreme power in a state, commanding what is right and prohibiting what is wrong.' Properties: it is a rule (permanent, uniform, universal), a rule of civil conduct (distinguishes from moral/religious law), prescribed (not secret; promulgated), and made by the supreme power in the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets multiple necessary attributes for municipal law: permanence/universality (not a one-off act), civil orientation (concerns citizen duties), publicity/prescription (must be promulgated before enforcement), and origin in supreme authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promulgation and publicity requirement for laws
rubrics_metrics.description: It is requisite that this resolution be notified to the people who are to obey it ... It may be notified by universal tradition and long practice ... viva voce ... by writing, printing, or the like; ... it is incumbent on the promulgators to do it in the most public and perspicuous manner ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lawmakers must make laws publicly known in a clear manner; methods vary (tradition, proclamation, publication); obscurity (tiny script, high placement) is condemned; ignorance is generally not a legitimate excuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of ex post facto laws; laws must operate in futuro
rubrics_metrics.description: There is still a more unreasonable method than this, which is called making of laws ex post facto; when after an action is committed, the legislator then for the first time declares it to have been a crime ... All laws should be therefore made to commence in futuro, and be notified before their commencement; which is implied in the term 'prescribed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declares retroactive criminalization unjust and cruel; requires laws to be prospective and notified prior to their operation so subjects can conform their conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between law, counsel, compact, and sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: A law is called a 'rule' to distinguish it from advice or counsel (which operate only on the willing), from a compact (a promise proceeding from us), and from a particular sentence or act (which affects only an individual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies conceptual boundaries: law is binding on the unwilling, a compact stems from mutual promise, counsel is persuasive, and particular legislative acts that affect only one person are sentences rather than laws.
